newsitem.title: UK: ISO sees world sugar prices falling to 10 cents/lb.
newsitem.headline: ISO sees world sugar prices falling to 10 cents/lb.

text.p: World sugar prices should eventually succumb to the pressure of a hefty statistical surplus in the 1996/97 crop year and drift lower to around 10 cents a pound, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said.
In its September market report, the ISO said a number of factors would restrain the bearish potential of the global balance -- but the effect of supply would win through.

These included the continuing relative tightness of standard quality white sugar, fears of a possible reduction of Brazilian supply from the next crop starting May 1997 and expectations of higher import demand from Russia.

"Nevertheless, we expect that the bearish fundamental situation will eventually overcome these limiting factors so that the world market enters a period of lower prices, close to the long term average of around 10 cents/lb," the ISO said.
World raw sugar prices are currently hovering around 10.80 cents/lb for delivery in March and May 1997.
The ISO said world production should reach 123.8 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, 200,000 up on 1995/96.
It said global consumption was expected to rise by 2.7 million tonnes to 121.3 million, leaving a statistical surplus of 2.5 million tonnes.
